findings.title: Drive metadata update has no tests
findings.description: The upload path now has separate branches to merge Drive URL and upload time into existing metadata or create a sidecar when none exists, but google_drive.rs has no tests for either branch. The pipeline metadata tests do not cover this code. A regression could lose the Drive link or overwrite existing voice fields while the upload itself still succeeds, leaving the Library unable to show the uploaded state.

findings.title: Remove the repeated scan documentation
findings.description: These adjacent comments describe the same responsibility in different words, so the second line adds no constraint or rationale and creates needless documentation to maintain. Keep one description or remove both if the function name is sufficient.

findings.title: Library and pipeline resolve different output directories
findings.description: This new resolver duplicates the pipeline's output-directory decision but treats an existing configured path as usable without attempting to create or write to it. The pipeline falls back when create_dir_all fails, so with an existing but unwritable configured directory recordings are saved under the fallback while the Library scans the configured directory and appears empty. Move output-directory resolution to a shared helper that both commands use, including the pipeline's create failure behavior.

findings.title: Recording deletion and sidecar cleanup are untested
findings.description: The new delete command removes the MP4 plus its metadata, transcript, and cached thumbnail, but the added tests only cover path validation and scanning; none exercise this command or its filesystem effects. A regression could leave stale companion files or report success/failure incorrectly without any test detecting it. Add a temporary-directory test that verifies all associated files are removed and that an invalid/outside path leaves them untouched.

findings.quote: const bytes = await tauriInvoke<number[]>('read_file_bytes', { path: thumbPath });
findings.title: Thumbnails fail when recordings use a custom output directory
findings.description: If a user sets `output_dir` to a location outside the temp, Videos, and `~/VoiceOver` directories, the pipeline and `generate_thumbnail` can write recordings and thumbnails there, but this `read_file_bytes` call is rejected by the existing command's path allowlist. The catch below leaves each card on its 🎬 placeholder, so thumbnails never display for recordings in otherwise supported custom locations.

findings.title: Revoke thumbnail object URLs when cards unmount
findings.description: Each visible recording card creates a blob URL for its thumbnail, but the onMount cleanup only disconnects the observer and never revokes that URL. Removing cards after deletion or leaving the Library leaves their blobs retained by the browser for the app session; a late thumbnail response can also allocate a URL after the card has unmounted. Revoke the URL during teardown and avoid publishing it after teardown.

findings.title: Library sorting has no regression tests
findings.description: The new LibraryState adds three sort modes and ascending/descending direction, but the changed feature adds no frontend tests for these results. The Rust scan test only checks that timestamps are non-increasing; it cannot catch a broken UI sort mode or direction toggle, so recordings could appear in the wrong order while the Library still renders normally.

findings.title: Release preview video blob URL on route teardown
findings.description: The Tauri preview reads the entire recording into a Blob and registers a blob URL, but this page has no teardown that revokes the URL. Navigating to a new recording or another route drops the component while the browser still retains the recording data through the object URL, so repeated previews can accumulate large video blobs for the lifetime of the app. Track and revoke the URL when the preview unmounts.

findings.title: Remove unused duplicate local voice setter
findings.description: This function has no callers anywhere in the project, and its body duplicates the used `setDefaultLocalVoice` immediately below. Keeping both leaves dead code and makes it unclear which setter owns local voice selection; delete this unused duplicate.
